indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B3.1.2.1: Recognize materials as important resources for providing human needs
indicator.objective: Identify the uses of everyday materials and link the uses to their properties

skills.description: Identify the uses of everyday materials
Link a property of a material to its use
Match an object to the material it is made from and explain why
Choose the best explanation of why a material is used for a specific purpose

misconceptions: Glass is used because it is pretty, not because it is transparent.
Metal is used for pots because it is shiny, not because it conducts heat.
Any material can be used for any purpose.
Plastic is always better than wood.
Clay is used for pots because it is soft, not because it can be moulded and baked hard.

questions.stem: What is wood commonly used for?
options: Making furniture like tables and chairs
questions.explanation: Wood is commonly used to make furniture like tables and chairs.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think wood is only used for burning.

questions.stem: What is glass commonly used for?
questions.explanation: Glass is commonly used for window panes because it lets light in.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse glass with plastic.

questions.stem: Why is metal used for making cooking pots?
hints: The heat needs to reach the food.
questions.explanation: Metal is used for cooking pots because it conducts heat well, allowing the food to cook.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think metal is used just because it is shiny.

questions.stem: Why is clay used for making pots?
options: Because it is bendable and can be moulded
Because it is waterproof when dry
hints: Clay is soft and wet at first.
You can shape it with your hands.
questions.explanation: Clay is used for pots because it can be moulded into shapes before it is baked hard.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think clay is used because it is hard.

questions.stem: Which material is best for making a raincoat because it keeps water out?
hints: It must not soak up water.
questions.explanation: Plastic is used for raincoats because it is waterproof and keeps the rain out.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think any cloth keeps water out.

questions.stem: Which property of glass makes it suitable for windows?
questions.explanation: Glass is transparent, allowing light to enter the room and people to see outside.
questions.misconception: Pupils may say glass is used because it is smooth.

questions.stem: Ama wants to make a bucket to carry water. Which material should she use?
hints: It must not tear or break easily.
questions.explanation: Plastic is a good material for a bucket because it is strong and waterproof.
questions.misconception: Pupils may choose glass because it holds water, but it breaks easily.

questions.stem: Kwame needs to cut a piece of paper. Which material is best for making a tool to cut it?
hints: The tool needs to be sharp.
questions.explanation: Metal is used for cutting tools like scissors because it can be made sharp and hard.
questions.misconception: Pupils may choose wood because it is hard, but it cannot be made sharp enough easily.

questions.stem: Why is cloth used for making clothes?
hints: You need to move your body.
questions.explanation: Cloth is used for clothes because it is soft and bendable, making it comfortable to wear.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not link comfort to the property of being soft.

questions.stem: Which material is used to make a tyre for a car?
hints: It must be strong and bendable.
questions.explanation: Rubber is used for tyres because it is strong, bendable, and grips the road well.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think metal is best because it is strong, but metal would be too hard and slippery.

questions.stem: Why is plastic commonly used for making water bottles?
options: Because it is light and waterproof
questions.explanation: Plastic is used for water bottles because it is light (easy to carry) and waterproof (holds liquid).
questions.misconception: Pupils may not consider weight as a property.

questions.stem: Name one use of metal in the home.
hints: What are your spoons made of?
questions.explanation: Metal is used for cooking pots, spoons, and many other items in the home.

questions.stem: Why is a sponge used for bathing? (Hint: Think about its property)
hints: What happens when you put it in water?
questions.explanation: A sponge is used for bathing because it is soft on the skin and absorbs water and soap.
questions.misconception: Pupils may say it is used because it is colourful.

questions.stem: Ama wants to buy a cup that will not break if she drops it. Which material should she choose?
questions.explanation: Plastic is a better choice than glass or clay because it is less likely to break when dropped.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all cups are made of glass.

questions.stem: Why is wood a better material for a cooking spoon than metal?
options: Wood does not get as hot as metal, so it is safer to hold
questions.explanation: Wood is a poor conductor of heat, so the handle of a wooden spoon does not get as hot as a metal one, making it safer to use.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think metal is better for all kitchen tools.

questions.stem: Why do we use glass for car windshields instead of wood?
options: Glass is transparent, allowing the driver to see the road
hints: The driver needs to see clearly.
questions.explanation: Glass is used because it is transparent and lets the driver see the road, whereas wood is opaque.
questions.misconception: Pupils may focus on strength rather than visibility.

questions.stem: Explain why clay is a good material for making a water pot.

criteria.description: States that clay can be moulded into shape
States that when baked, it becomes hard and can hold water

hints: Can you shape clay with your hands?
What happens when it is baked in a fire?
questions.explanation: Clay is mouldable when wet, so it can be shaped into a pot. When baked, it becomes hard and waterproof enough to hold water.

questions.stem: A tailor needs to make a school bag. Write down one material the tailor could use and explain why its properties make it suitable.

criteria.description: Names a suitable material (e.g., cloth, leather, plastic)
Explains a property that makes it suitable (e.g., strong, bendable, waterproof)

hints: Does it need to be strong?
questions.explanation: Cloth is suitable because it is strong and bendable, allowing it to hold books without tearing.

questions.stem: Why would a metal bucket be BAD for carrying hot water, while a plastic bucket might also be bad?
options: Metal conducts heat (gets hot quickly) and plastic might melt or soften
Metal is too heavy and plastic is too light
Metal is transparent and plastic is opaque
hints: Think about holding a hot metal pot.
questions.explanation: Metal conducts heat quickly, making it dangerous to hold. Plastic may soften or melt when in contact with very hot water. Both have drawbacks for hot water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not consider the effect of heat on plastic.

questions.stem: A company wants to make a cheap, light, and waterproof raincoat. Which material is most suitable?
hints: It must be light to wear.
questions.explanation: A thin plastic sheet is cheap, light, and waterproof, making it ideal for a cheap raincoat.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think leather is best, but it is heavy and expensive.
